title: Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv Bridge as Germany's Merz Arrives to Sirens
excerpt: Merz landed in Kyiv to pledge €1 billion in military aid and a joint drone-production deal as Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial targets.
body:
• A Russian drone struck Kyiv's Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge on Sunday morning as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the Ukrainian capital to air raid sirens, explosions and air-defence fire. Kyiv's mayor said two people were injured.
  • Merz is in Kyiv to pledge support to President Volodymyr Zelensky, with German officials saying he will announce €1 billion ($1.13 billion) in military aid, €350 million for energy-sector repairs and a joint drone-production deal.
  • Zelensky said Russia launched 135 attack drones overnight, more than 50 of them jet-powered, and had used more than 1,900 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 25 missiles against Ukraine in the past week alone.
  • The strike was the second hit on the Northern Bridge in two days. Ukraine's infrastructure minister said Kyiv would begin building alternative crossings over the Dnipro if attacks on the bridges continue.

KYIV: A Russian drone slammed into a major bridge in Kyiv on Sunday as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the Ukrainian capital to the sound of air raid sirens, explosions and air-defence systems opening fire — a stark backdrop for a visit meant to demonstrate European support as Russia escalates its strikes on the city.

Video footage from Sunday morning showed the moment the Pivnichnyi Bridge, the capital's Northern Bridge across the Dnipro River, was hit, sending a huge plume of fire and black smoke into the air while cars were still travelling across it. Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the strike damaged the bridge's roadway and a hot-water supply system, injuring two people. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck the bridge, claiming it was targeting a route used for transporting troops and military equipment.

A visit timed for escalation

Merz is in Kyiv to display support for President Volodymyr Zelensky amid Russia's intensifying campaign against the capital. "Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks," Merz said on arrival, warning that "if Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us."

"If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us."

— Friedrich Merz, German Chancellor

German officials said Merz will announce €1 billion ($1.13 billion) in military aid and €350 million for repairs in Ukraine's battered energy sector, alongside a joint drone-production deal due to be finalised during the visit. He is accompanied by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and executives from Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence and Quantum Systems.

The two leaders visited the damaged building of Ukraine's Academy of Sciences, where at least two people died in a drone strike last week. "I can only repeat it once again from this point: Mr Putin, put an end to this senseless war," Merz said. "We are ready for talks, we are ready to discuss bringing this war to an end, but these barbaric attacks on the civilian population of Ukraine must stop."

The bridge campaign

Sunday's strike was the second hit on the Northern Bridge in two days. On Thursday and Friday, Kyiv's Pivdennyi, or Southern Bridge — which serves ground transportation and the city's subway system — was struck five times in less than 24 hours, according to Ukrainian officials.

Ukrainian officials say the strikes aim to cut Kyiv in two along the Dnipro River, which separates government and business districts on the right bank from largely residential areas on the left. The infrastructure minister said on Sunday that the city planned to build several alternative crossings if the attacks continue. Russia's defence ministry, meanwhile, said its forces would intensify strikes on "military and military-industrial facilities, as well as related infrastructure" in Kyiv and other regions — a statement issued after Zelensky vowed to step up attacks on Russian oil refineries. The ministry added that two cargo vessels carrying military equipment to Odesa's port were struck, and said a logistics centre in the Kyiv region was targeted on Saturday.

A week of relentless strikes

Zelensky, who shared footage of the bridge attack on X, said Russian forces also hit a pharmaceutical warehouse in Sumy, killing one person, and a communications facility in Dnipro, injuring six in the overnight attacks. "It is important that Ukraine is not left alone against this terror," he said. "This week alone, the Russians have used more than 1,900 attack drones, 1,700 aerial bombs, and 25 missiles against Ukraine."

What's next

Four air raid alerts sounded across Kyiv on Sunday morning. The immediate test of Merz's visit is the finalisation of the drone-production deal and the release of the €1 billion aid package, which Zelensky says Ukraine needs to field air defences capable of intercepting Russia's newer jet-powered drones. For Kyiv's residents, the longer question is whether the bridge campaign will permanently reshape how the divided city moves. Germany is home to Europe's largest Ukrainian refugee population and a large Indian diaspora, both watching how the aid and energy-repair commitments affect Berlin's defence spending and winter energy costs.
